summary: Ronald Egan is a sinologist who earned his Ph.D. at Harvard University (~1972–1977). He held posts at Harvard (~1977–1986), Wellesley College, the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1994–2012), and Stanford University (~2012–2022).

Ronald M. Davidson specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, earning his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley by 1985. He studied under numerous scholars and traditional teachers, and held a post at Fairfield University (attested 2002–2005).

Ronald Neufeldt is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held posts at the University of Calgary as Associate Professor in the Religious Studies Department (~1976–1990) and continued there from ~1990 to 2006.

Ronald Y. Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1974–1980). He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1991) and the Pacific School of Religion (attested 1996).

Rong Ma works in Tibetology and other fields. He earned a doctorate in social geography from Brown University, served as a visiting scholar at Harvard University, and directed Peking University's Institute of Sociology and Anthropology (attested 1998).

Rongdao Lai specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, completing a PhD at McGill University (attested 2013) under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates. She was also a visiting fellow at the Center for Chinese Studies.
Rory Brendan Lindsay is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Toronto and earned his PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.
Rory Mackenzie works in Buddhist studies and religious studies, having completed his doctoral studies under Peter Harvey. He has held a post as a teacher at International Christian College.
Rosan Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and served as a professor there from ~1986 to 2012.

Rosane Rocher is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the Free University of Brussels (~1955–1961). She served as Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (~1970–2004), where she became Professor Emerita of South Asia Studies around 2004.

Rosemarie Fuchs is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under Katia Holmes and traditional teacher Khenpo Tsültrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, and was a member of the Marpa Translation Committee (attested 2000).
Rosemarie Lühr is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who held posts at the University of Giessen (~1990–1992) and the University of Jena (~1992–2013).

Rosina Pastore is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Lausanne under supervisors Maya Burger and Stefania Cavaliere. She also worked as an assistant and PhD candidate at Lausanne.
Roy Rappaport worked in religious studies and other fields. He studied at Columbia University (~1959–1966) and held a post at the University of Michigan from ~1965 to 1997.

Roy Tzohar works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tel Aviv University (~1997–2004) and completed his PhD at Columbia University (~2004–2011) under Gary A. Tubb. He joined Tel Aviv University in ~2011.

Royall Tyler works in Japanology and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1953–1957) and Columbia University (~1965–1977), and held posts at the University of Oslo (~1983–1990) and the Australian National University (~1990–2000).
Royce Wiles is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the Australian National University by 2000 and held a post there.

Ruben L. F. Habito works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1973–1984) under Akira Hirakawa and Jikido Takasaki, and held posts at Sophia University (~1981–1989) and Southern Methodist University (~1989–2020).

Rudolf von Roth was an Indologist and linguist who studied theology at Tübinger Stift under Heinrich Ewald (~1839–1843) and under Eugène Burnouf (~1843–1844). He spent his career at the University of Tübingen (1848–1895).

Ruixuan Chen specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under MA supervisor Jens-Uwe Hartmann, earned his PhD at Leiden University under Paul Harrison (attested 2018), and held a post at Heidelberg University.
